items.title: Imran being forced into Benazir, Nawaz-style deal, claims Achakzai
items.description: • Demands authorities disclose whereabouts of Sohail Afridi • Mengal says those claiming to be framers of Constitution are ‘trampling it’ • TTAP alliance challenges governor’s rule, emergency before Peshawar High Court PESHAWAR: PTI fou­nder Imran Khan is being forced into an agreement, similar to those given to former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto, Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai claimed on Friday. The opposition leader was referring to the arrangements whereby the two former PMs went into self-imposed exile following their respective ousters. Mr Sharif, who was ousted and imprisoned following a military coup by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf, left the country in 2000 following a deal negotiated by Saudi and Lebanese leaders. Benazir, meanwhile, voluntarily went into self-exile after her party lost the 1997 general elections following her dismissal by then-president Farooq Leg­hari. At the time, her husband Asif Zardari was imprisoned over corruption charges, and was finally released in 2004. “The same is happening today with the PML-N and PPP in government,” Mr Achakzai said at a news conference at the Peshawar High Court (PHC). He was accompanied by Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) leaders Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. He said they were in contact with all opposition parties and would soon convene a multi-party conference. Resigning from the assemblies was also an option, he said, adding that they had submitted their demands in response to the offer of negotiations. “Nowhere in the world is a prisoner denied meetings,” he said, calling for the withdrawal of the “wrong amen­dment”, empow­erment of parliament and the formation of an independent commission to ensure transparent elections. He said no problem could be resolved until parliament was empowered. Expressing concern over the whereabouts of the KP chief minister and other lawmakers, he demanded that the authorities disclose the chief minister’s whereabouts, calling it their constitutional right to know. “We stand with the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The people of this province have the first right over its minerals. Regardless of political affiliation, everyone must unite for the homeland,” he said, adding that they would be safer if the country survived. Mr Mengal said those claiming to be the framers of the Constitution were trampling on it. He questioned the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on the grounds of terrorism, asking whether military operations had improved or worsened conditions in Balochistan. He said KP’s elected chief minister had been removed, while the provincial assembly speaker and a minister were missing. Those who had won the general elections on Form 47 had become members of the National Assembly, he alleged, adding that the system could not continue this way. Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had reached its peak. “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” he told reporters, adding that a cabinet member had himself acknowledged that the system had collapsed. TTAP challenges governor’s rule Meanwhile on Friday, TTAP leaders challenged the proclamation of emergency and imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before the PHC, seeking to have the measures declared unconstitutional and illegal. The constitutional petition was jointly filed by TTAP Chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Vice Chairman Senator Raja Nasir Abbas, Balochistan National Party-Mengal chief Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Sindh Taraqi Pasand Party leader Syed Zainul Abideen through Advocates Muazzam Butt and Baseem Ahmad Siddiqui. The court was requested to declare the Oct 11 proclamation of emergency, issued under Articles 232(1) and 234 of the Constitution, unconstitutional and without lawful authority, arguing that the required constitutional conditions had not been met or that the measures exceeded the powers conferred by the Constitution. They challenged the purported transfer of the KP Assembly’s legislative powers to parliament and the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet. They also sought the annulment of executive orders and notifications that depended on the validity of the proclamation. The petitioners also challenged the establishment of the purported KP Advisory Council and Area Development Secretariat, arguing that these bodies could not exercise powers beyond those conferred by the Constitution or replace established provincial institutions. They questioned any purported suspension of constitutional provisions, including Article 175(3), unless expressly authorised by the Constitution. The petitioners sought annulment of the Oct 11 notification concerning the deployment of armed forces in the province to the extent where it violated Article 245, failed to meet constitutional requirements or exceeded the scope of the provision. They also sought directions to ensure that elected representatives and constitutionally established institutions in KP were not unlawfully prevented from performing their functions and that no elected representative was detained or restrained except in accordance with the Constitution. Pending a final decision, they sought interim relief to suspend or restrain the impugned measures to prevent the displacement of elected institutions, transfer of legislative authority, creation of parallel executive structures or other irreparable harm, subject to the court’s assessment of constitutional requirements and public safety. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan rules out unconditional talks with Afghanistan
items.description: • Demands verifiable mechanism to end terrorist attacks from Afghan soil • FO says no formal Russian mediation initiative currently under discussion • Warns India that any future aggression will be met with a stronger response ISLAMABAD: The Foreign Office on Friday said that talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional, while rejecting suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour and saying it would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute. “Pakistan is not shying away from discussions or dialogue, including with representatives of Afghanistan. Pakistan would welcome any sincere efforts by friendly countries that could help address our legitimate security concerns and promoting regional peace and stability,” Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at the weekly media briefing. The statement came as Russia recently renewed its readiness to mediate between the two countries, although Islamabad denied the existence of any such initiative. “At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion,” Mr Khan said, adding that Pakistan remained open to engagement that produced tangible results. Russia, the only country to have formally recognised the Taliban government, has recently renewed its offer to facilitate a settlement if both sides request its involvement. Moscow’s special envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, had earlier this month made this suggestion after the latest round of the Moscow Format consultations on Oct 5 ended without a joint communiqué because of differences between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban delegations over references to terrorist networks operating from Afghanistan. Mr Khan said the absence of an agreed statement at the Moscow Format meeting reflected the Afghan delegation’s unwillingness to accept language on terrorist networks that had been agreed in the previous year’s document. “The fact that no joint communiqué was issued after the Moscow Format is self-evident that Afghanistan did not accept the formulation which had been acceptable until last year particularly about presence of terrorist network in Afghanistan. This shows that there is reluctance on the part of Afghanistan that terrorism is originating from its soil,” he said. The failure to get a joint communique highlighted the central obstacle to normalising relations, which is Pakistan’s demand for action against the Tehreek-i-Taliban Paki­stan (TTP) and other terrorist groups it says are using Afghan territory to launch attacks across the border. The Taliban authorities have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan. The dispute has frustrated international efforts to reduce tensions. Qatar and Turkiye last October helped broker a ceasefire, but subsequent round of talks failed to reach a lasting settlement. Saudi Arabia separately hosted discussions, while China held talks between the two sides in Urumqi in April. None of these efforts could resolve the disagreement over terrorist groups and the measures needed to prevent cross border attacks. Pakistan’s position, Mr Khan said, was that dialogue would need to be backed by an arrangement that could verify whether terrorist activity against the country had stopped. “The talks will not be unconditional. Pakistan has been raising the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan at different forums. Unfortunately, the Taliban regime has been taking one step forward and one step backward,” Mr Khan emphasised. “Pakistan has only one demand that there should be a verifiable mechanism to ensure complete cessation of terrorist activities emanating from Afghan soil against Pakistan,” he said. ‘Stronger response’ Mr Khan reminded India of the response it faced during last year’s military confrontation and warned that any future aggression would be met with an even stronger response. FO reaction came after Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh a day earlier threatened a bigger strike in the event of any future terrorist attacks. Singh, while speaking at National Defence Conclave 2026 in Delhi, recalled Operation Sindoor and said that it marked a decisive response to terrorism. He also referred to earlier Indian military operations. “We reject and condemn the Indian Defence Minister’s provocative remarks entailing a threat of Indian aggression against Pakistan. Such reckless statements reflect India’s hegemonistic mindset and the risks its belligerent posture poses to regional peace and stability in South Asia,” Mr Khan said. “We wish to remind India of the consequences of its military aggression in May last year, when Pakistan demonstrated both its capability and resolve to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and gave a fitting reply to Indian aggression,” the FO spokesperson said. Mr Khan urged New Delhi to draw lessons from the previous confrontation and avoid further escalation. “India should draw an appropriate lesson from the last year’s experience and abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric and act with responsibility for lasting peace in the region,” he said. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

Les troubles ont mis à l'épreuve les forces de l'ordre et endommagé de nombreuses infrastructures. Pour le Premier ministre Navin Ramgoolam, qui s'est exprimé sur le sujet, ces violences pourraient être liées à des réseaux de trafiquants de drogue. Une piste qui s'ajoute aux tensions provoquées par la vie chère, les difficultés d'accès à l'eau et une grave blessure par balle impliquant un policier.

items.title: Ablakwa challenges Minority to identify an evacuee denied GH¢5,500 allowance
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has challenged the Minority in Parliament to identify a Ghanaian evacuated from South Africa who did not receive the GH¢5,500 allowance, dismissing allegations of unaccounted funds as attempts to create a scandal. The government evacuated Ghanaians from South Africa following heightened anti-immigrant sentiment and attacks targeting foreign nationals in the country. The operation ended on September 4, 2026, after three days, according to Mr Ablakwa. He said his September 7 briefing was intended to provide an account of the exercise to the public. Mr Ablakwa said the evacuation exercise ended on September 4, 2026, and that he briefed the press three days later to account for the operation. He questioned claims that some people on the evacuation list could not be traced and that the funds allocated for the exercise had not been fully accounted for. “All of that propaganda out there that some people on the list cannot be found and that some voodoo analysis they have done showed that there’s some money that has not been accounted for,” he said. The Minister said he had been looking for an evacuee who could publicly state that they did not receive the allowance. “I have been looking for one Ghanaian to step forward and say that when we were evacuated from South Africa, the 5,500 Cedi reintegration allowance I didn’t get it as a Ghanaian. Or the 500 Cedi transportation allowance, I didn’t get it. Have you heard of any one Ghanaian? One,” he said. He questioned why the evacuation had become controversial, insisting there was no scandal to uncover. “So what is this desperate attempt to create a scandal when there is none? When the whole world is commending that all of that propaganda…” he said. His remarks came in response to concerns over the handling of the evacuation, including questions about individuals listed as beneficiaries and the disbursement of funds. The dispute centres on the government’s management of the evacuation and the use of public funds to support returning Ghanaians. While Mr Ablakwa maintains that the allowances were paid, the Minority’s concerns include the whereabouts of some individuals on the evacuation list and whether all expenditure has been properly accounted for.

items.title: L’AES définit ses priorités lors des négociations avec les pays de la CEDEAO dans les prochains jours à Dakar
items.description: L'Alliance des États du Sahel a défini vendredi trois priorités pour ses négociations avec la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO), prévues les 17 et 18 octobre prochains à Dakar. Dans un communiqué, le ministère burkinabé des Affaires étrangères a indiqué que les priorités de l’Alliance consistent à préserver la souveraineté des États, à renforcer la confédération et à défendre les intérêts des populations. Cette annonce a été faite lors d’une réunion des ministres des Affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger, à Ouagadougou, visant à coordonner les positions des trois pays en vue des premières consultations officielles entre l’Alliance et la CEDEAO. Les ministres des Affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré, Abdoulaye Diop et Bakary Yao Sangaré, ont réaffirmé leur attachement au respect de la souveraineté de leurs pays, soulignant l’importance de préserver les liens historiques entre les peuples de la région du Sahel et le reste des pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Ils ont également souligné l’importance de la libre circulation des personnes et des marchandises, et ont exprimé leur volonté d’adopter une approche fondée sur la responsabilité, le respect mutuel et la prise en compte des intérêts des populations, appelant à la recherche de solutions africaines aux défis régionaux. Fondée en 2023, l’Alliance des États du Sahel regroupe le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger ; ces trois pays se sont officiellement retirés de la CEDEAO en janvier 2025. Les négociations de Dakar s’inscrivent dans le cadre des efforts déployés par ces trois pays pour renforcer leur autonomie politique et institutionnelle et définir la nature de leurs relations futures avec la CEDEAO.

items.title: Debate, leadership and governance drew me to politics – Ekua Amoakoh
items.description: Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, says her lifelong interest in debate, governance and leadership inspired her to pursue a career in politics. In a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, she said she had always been vocal about how institutions and society should be run and wanted to contribute to decisions affecting Ghana’s development. “I always enjoyed debates and, you know, governance. And I always had opinions on stuff. So I think that’s why I wanted to be a politician. I always had opinions on what to do, how everything should be run,” she said. Dr Amoakoh said she frequently found herself in leadership positions during her education, from junior secondary school through senior secondary school. “At every point in my life, whether in JSS or secondary school, I always end up in some position of leadership because I’m very verbose,” she said. She recalled an incident from medical school involving a lecturer known among students as “Captain”, whom she described as intimidating. Dr Amoakoh said students were sometimes too frightened to approach him with difficult issues, prompting them to ask her to speak on their behalf. “We all needed to tell Captain something that he really wouldn’t understand. But everybody was just too frightened to tell him. They’d say, ‘Akua, go and do it,’” she recounted. She said the experience reflected a pattern in her life in which she often became the person expected to speak up when others were reluctant to do so. “So I always knew that I always had that ability to be able to speak when I needed to. And I had opinions on everything,” she said. Dr Amoakoh said her political ambition was also driven by a desire to contribute directly to Ghana’s development. She explained that she did not want to remain outside the decision-making process when she believed she could help shape the country’s direction. “I didn’t want to be in a position where I couldn’t influence the growth of this country, for instance,” she said.

items.title: Éthiopie: le gouvernement fédéral installe une administration intérimaire au Tigré pour six mois
items.description: En Éthiopie, c'est désormais officiel : le gouvernement fédéral reprend le contrôle administratif du Tigré. Il a annoncé vendredi 16 octobre la mise en place d'une administration intérimaire pour six mois. Les autorités fédérales reprennent ainsi formellement l'administration de cette région, jusqu'ici dirigée par les rebelles du Front de libération du peuple du Tigré (TPLF). Après plusieurs semaines de combats contre l'armée fédérale, les troupes du TPLF ont été repoussées vers le nord et ont perdu le contrôle des grandes villes de la région.

items.title: Japanese PM sends ritual offering to war-linked Yasukuni Shrine
items.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Saturday sent a ritual offering to the war-linked Yasukuni Shrine as its three-day autumn festival began, local media reported. Takaichi sent a potted plant offering known as "masakaki" to the notorious shrine, a symbol of Japanese militarism and wartime aggression, under her title as prime minister, Kyodo News reported. Takaichi, a conservative politician who regularly visited the controversial shrine before becoming prime minister, is unlikely to visit it during the current festival, the report said, citing a source close to her. While serving as a minister, Takaichi visited the shrine during its spring and autumn festivals and on August 15, the anniversary of Japan's surrender in World War II. However, she has refrained from doing so since becoming prime minister on October 21 last year. Yasukuni Shrine, located in central Tokyo's Chiyoda Ward, honors 14 convicted Japanese Class-A war criminals from World War II. It has long been a source of diplomatic friction between Japan and its neighbors. For a long time, visits and ritual offerings made by Japanese officials to the shrine have consistently sparked criticism and opposition both at home and abroad, hurting the feelings of the people of China, South Korea, and other countries and regions victimized by Japan's wartime aggression.

items.title: La garde à vue des suspects dans l’affaire des « blogueurs de l’étranger » : le parquet s’explique
items.description: Le parquet général mauritanien a déclaré que les mesures prises dans le cadre de l'enquête préliminaire relative à l'affaire des « blogueurs de l'étranger », transmise à la Direction de la sécurité d'État, respectaient les garanties constitutionnelles et légales, en réponse aux critiques concernant la durée de la garde à vue et le droit des suspects à consulter leur avocat. Dans un communiqué publié ce vendredi, le parquet a précisé que la loi exclut les suspects de crimes contre la sécurité de l’État et de terrorisme du droit de contacter leur avocat pendant toute la durée de la garde à vue, conformément au dernier alinéa de l’article régissant ce droit dans le Code de procédure pénale, sans pour autant porter atteinte aux autres garanties juridiques qui leur sont accordées. Ce communiqué fait suite à des critiques relayées sur les réseaux sociaux concernant les mesures prises dans le cadre de cette affaire, notamment celles relatives à l’interdiction faite à des avocats de rencontrer les personnes placées en garde à vue dans ce dossier. Le parquet a souligné que l’article 8 du Code de procédure pénale impose de préserver la dignité des personnes privées de liberté et interdit de les exposer à des mauvais traitements ou à la torture. Il a ajouté qu’il supervisait l’action de la police judiciaire afin de garantir le respect de ces dispositions et de toutes les garanties prévues aux différentes étapes de l’enquête, depuis l’arrestation des suspects jusqu’à leur renvoi devant lui. Le parquet a déclaré qu’il continuerait à veiller au respect des délais de garde à vue fixés par la loi en fonction de la nature des infractions, et à prendre les mesures judiciaires prévues à l’expiration de ces délais. Il a réaffirmé que l’application de la loi, la sauvegarde des droits et libertés ainsi que la protection de l’ordre public sont des responsabilités qu’il assume en toute indépendance et impartialité, et que les mesures prises restent soumises aux règles de procédure et aux garanties prévues par la loi.

items.title: Rabies death toll rises to 40 in Sindh after elderly man dies
items.description: KARACHI: A septuagenarian man died of rabies at a local hospital, raising this year’s tally from the deadly infectious disease in Sindh to 40, officials said on Friday. They said that the victim, a resident of Baldia Town, was bitten by a dog over three weeks back but he did not seek preventive treatment. He passed away at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) on Thursday. The JPMC has recorded over 11,000 dog bite cases and 10 deaths from rabies this year, including the latest one. Recently, a 38-year-old man hailing from Diplo, Tharparkar, and a 12-year-old boy hailing from Hyderabad died of rabies. Experts say a large number of rabies cases go unreported as patients use home remedies or turn to faith healers for “treatment”. They emphasised the need for public awareness, humane control of the dog population and the availability of appropriate treatment in hospitals. While dog bites account for the majority of rabies cases, bites from potentially rabid wild animals can also transmit the virus. After exposure, early wound cleansing, timely rabies vaccination and the administration of rabies immunoglobulin, if needed, can effectively prevent the disease, which is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms appear. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

items.title: SC questions ‘lofty expectations’ in criminal cases
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court has taken exception to a prevalent practice in criminal trials which, it said, defied normal human capability and natural perception, and observed that eyewitness accounts should reflect genuine human observation rather than physically impossible details concerning firearm incidents. “To expect mathematical precision regarding the number of firearm shots or the exact location of injuries from eyewitnesses exposed to a horrific event is both unnatural and impractical,” observed Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim in a judgement he authored. Justice Ibrahim was a member of a three-judge SC bench headed by Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, which took up criminal appeals filed by Muhammad Azhar and the state challenging a Sept 13, 2021, Lahore High Court, Bahawalpur, ruling. The SC, however, rejected the criminal appeal in the 2017 murder case, upholding Muhammad Azhar’s conviction for killing Sakhian Bibi. Expecting mathematical precision from eyewitnesses exposed to traumatic events is ‘unnatural and impractical’, Justice Ibrahim holds “In criminal jurisprudence, human behaviour should not be subjected to a fixed formula, nor should every witness be expected to react to, observe or retain events in an identical manner,” the judgement said. The incident occurred on Jan 11, 2017, when the appellant allegedly entered the victim’s home armed with a .30-bore pistol, seeking the complainant’s uncle in connection with ongoing civil litigation. When the victim said her uncle was not present, the petitioner opened fire, discharging five shots that struck her chest, abdomen and right arm. The additional sessions judge, Minch­inabad, convicted the petitioner and sentenced him to death, with Rs200,000 in compensation payable to the legal heirs. The LHC, Bahawalpur, later commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment, prompting both the petitioner’s appeal and the state’s petition for enhancement of the sentence. “We frequently observe prosecution witnesses deposing with microscopic precision, as if watching events in slow motion, describing the exact trajectory and anatomical landing site of each individual bullet discharged from a firearm,” the judgement observed. It is humanly impossible for an eyewitness exposed to the sudden terror and high stress of a deadly attack to track a high-velocity bullet in mid-air and confirm precisely where each shot strikes the victim’s body, it noted. The judge emphasised that every individual reacts differently to a sudden traumatic situation: while one person may observe details, another may freeze or lose awareness of the occurrence. In a sudden traumatic event, when multiple gunshots ring out within a few seconds and a mother is murdered in cold blood before her son’s eyes, a minor divergence regarding the exact number of firearm shots or the precise entry point of each bullet is evidence of natural and reasonable human limitations, he observed. It is common knowledge that most individuals are not frequently exposed to dangerous, life-threatening situations, and the sudden brandishing of a weapon induces an atmosphere of shock and fear, according to the judgement. In such stressful encounters, human cognitive and perceptual capacities are severely impaired, the judgement said. To substantiate this point, it cited renowned cognitive psychologist Elizabeth Loftus, who had stated that a witness confronted by an assailant brandishing a firearm involuntarily fixes their attention almost exclusively on the weapon itself. This cognitive phenomenon, known as “attentional tunnelling”, limits the observer’s capacity to process or recall surrounding details, the judgement said. Trial courts should bear these limitations in mind when scrutinising eyewitness accounts claiming microscopic accuracy despite the stressful circumstances, Justice Ibrahim observed. The judgement expected lower courts to assess witnesses in the light of the circumstances of each case, observing that, under the golden principles of criminal jurisprudence, no piece of evidence should be considered in isolation; rather, all evidence should be evaluated cumulatively alongside other available evidence. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

items.title: Terrorism has no link with Baloch values, says Bugti
items.description: QUETTA: Condemning a recent terrorist attack in Dasht Goran, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti said on Friday that the government had always maintained that such acts have nothing to do with Baloch values, rather were purely terrorism. He was responding to points raised by lawmakers on various issues in the Balochistan Assembly. Earlier, MPA Mir Jahanzeb Mengal, speaking on a point of order, said that “Fitna al-Hindustan” had attacked the house of Mir Qambar Khan Mengal in Dasht Goran at 6am. He said the firing continued until 4pm, leaving Ahmed Nawaz Mengal dead and another person injured. “This is my house, and my mother and sisters are there. This is not Balochiyat. If anyone is so keen on fighting, let them specify the place, field and time. The Balochistan chief minister should take notice of the incident,” he said. Condemns Dasht Goran attack; directs district administrations to inspect school and college buildings in Balochistan CM Bugti said the people of the province were increasingly realising that the Baloch were being pushed into a futile conflict. “What kind of tradition allows the killing of passengers and unarmed people?” he asked. Asma Jattak case Then, speaking about the high-profile Asma Jattak case, he said the government had been in contact with her family. “I have said before that the matter is sensitive and cannot be discussed on the floor of the assembly,” he said. The case he was referring to revolves around the murder of Ms Jattak’s father in August this year. The woman in question was abducted in 2025. After being freed, she levelled allegations against an influential individual, accusing him of threatening her family. The same day, her father was shot dead outside their residence. Referring to remarks by lawmakers during a previous sitting, the chief minister said it was inappropriate to name an individual, whose father had also served as the provincial chief minister, and allege on the assembly floor that those responsible for the killing of Asma Jattak’s father were present in the house. “I have reports from the security agencies, and the information provided by the member concerned is incorrect,” he said. School safety Referring to the recent school roof collapse incident in Peshawar where several children lost their lives, former chief minister Dr Abdul Malik Baloch urged the chief minister to direct the Education Department, the Communications and Works (C&W) Department and local councillors to inspect all government and private school buildings across Balochistan. He said officials should visit schools in every area and ensure that any building found to be dilapidated was closed until it could be made safe. In response, the chief minister said he had directed authorities to inspect the buildings of all schools and colleges across the province. Speaker Abdul Khaliq Khan Achak­­zai noted that because madressahs accommodate children, their buildings also require strict safety inspections. Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

items.title: ‘My Grandmother is an NPP Founding member’ – Ekua Amoakoh reveals family’s NPP roots
items.description: Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, has revealed that her grandmother was a founding member of the party and served as one of its early treasurers in the Ashanti Region. Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh said she spent considerable time with her grandmother while growing up and learnt a great deal from her. She described her grandmother as a politician who played a role in the NPP’s early organisation. “My grandma is a founding member of the NPP. She was one of the first people to be treasurer in Ashanti Region. She is a council of elders—like she is,” she said. Dr Amoakoh said she spent much of her childhood with her grandmother, particularly when her mother enrolled at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) to pursue further qualifications. She recounted the period humorously, suggesting that her mother’s studies gave her more time with her grandmother. “I spent a lot of time with my grandmother. And I think I learned a lot of things from her,” she said. Her account offers a glimpse into the family relationships that influenced her upbringing and her later involvement in politics. Dr Amoakoh’s account places her grandmother’s political involvement among the family experiences that preceded her own work with the NPP. The party was established in 1992 and draws from Ghana’s Danquah-Busia-Dombo political tradition. Her grandmother’s reported role as an early treasurer in the Ashanti Region points to a family association with the party dating back to its formative years. Dr Amoakoh also spoke about growing up at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, where her grandmother worked as Director of Nursing. She said her parents encouraged her to study medicine, although she initially resisted the decision and questioned her choice even after entering medical school. She has since come to appreciate the experience and the discipline it instilled in her. “I’m glad they insisted because even if it’s not something you are going to practice or something you are going to use, that whole process of training, I think it can forge any person into a formidable person,” she said. Dr Amoakoh’s interview on PM Express explored her childhood, family background and the experiences that helped shape her career in medicine and politics.

items.title: Aden airport hit; Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones, missiles
items.description: Ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group struck the international airport in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden on Friday night, Aden's security administration said, while the Saudi-led coalition said earlier it had intercepted fresh drones and missiles over Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea. Aden's security administration said in a statement that two missiles landed inside the grounds of Aden International Airport, with preliminary information indicating no casualties. A local security official earlier told Xinhua that two missiles had landed near Aden International Airport, while a third struck a military base near the headquarters of the Saudi-led coalition forces in Al Buraiqa district in western Aden. Three powerful explosions rocked the city, the temporary seat of the internationally recognized Yemeni government, during the attack, a Xinhua reporter on the ground and local residents said. Ambulances were seen heading toward the affected areas. Shortly after the attack, Houthi-run al-Masirah TV cited a military leader within the group as saying the group had targeted "the headquarters of Saudi forces and weapons depots" at Badr military camp near Aden International Airport. The attack came a day after missiles struck the Al-Ma'ashiq Presidential Palace compound in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the government. The Houthi group claimed responsibility for the attack, saying it had targeted a "Saudi military operations headquarters" inside the presidential palace compound. Earlier on Friday, the Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said coalition forces had intercepted and destroyed three drones in Saudi Arabia's southern region and the capital Riyadh region, as well as a fourth launched toward the Eastern Province. The forces had also intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and a ballistic missile launched toward Yanbu, a port city on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, the spokesperson said. The repeated attacks come amid an escalating exchange of strikes between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, a main ally of Yemen's government. The coalition said Thursday that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had killed 17 people and injured more than 330 others since October 1, with the airport coming under 20 attacks during the two-week period. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei reiterated Friday that Iran was ready to help resolve differences between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis "if requested by both sides," rejecting allegations that Tehran had played a role in Houthi operations, Iranian media reported. Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, forcing the government out of the capital.

items.title: Confédération AES : Une délégation unique des ministres en charge de la diplomatie pour les discussions avec la CEDEAO à Dakar
items.description: En prélude aux concertations avec la CEDEAO, les ministres en charge des affaires étrangères de la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) se sont réunis le vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, pour examiner les travaux préparatoires tenus les 14 et 15 octobre par les experts. En clair, il s'est agi pour ces responsables de la diplomatie d'harmoniser les points d'échanges avec la CEDEAO, dans un esprit de préservation de l'intérêt des populations africaines de façon générale. Les ministres ont réaffirmé l'attachement à rester dans la confédération AES et au noble combat que mènent les trois présidents dans la lutte pour la libération de l'espace. Pour situer le contexte, l'hôte de la réunion, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, ministre burkinabè des affaires étrangères, a rappelé deux étapes-clés. Il s'agit de la rencontre qu'ils ont, ministres en charge de la diplomatie, eue à Niamey, en février 2025, puis à Bamako, en mai 2025, avec une délégation de la CEDEAO, pour échanger sur les perspectives futures de coopération. « Cette rencontre a permis d'aboutir à un consensus, qui était d'observer un statu quo sur tout ce qui est acquis positif dans l'espace CEDEAO (je dirai, ex-espace CEDEAO) et qui porte sur la libre circulation et bien d'autres questions qui ont un bénéfice certain pour nos populations respectives. Cette réunion a aussi été l'occasion de valider les secteurs d'intérêts majeurs. Nous en avions retenu, en son temps, quatorze, sur lesquels nous devons poursuivre les négociations et aboutir à des instruments juridiques pour offrir de nouvelles bases de coopération. C'était aussi l'occasion de nous accorder sur l'organisation pratique des négociations ; comment les pays doivent mettre en place leurs équipes et comment la CEDEAO aussi va interagir avec nous. C'est ce qui a abouti à la nomination du négociateur en chef par la CEDEAO et à la mise en place d'une task force au niveau de l'espace confédéral avec des équipes techniques d'experts par pays, mais aussi des équipes pluridisciplinaires qui vont poursuivre le dialogue plus tard », retrace le ministre Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré avant de préciser que l'étape de Dakar s'inscrit en droite ligne de ce qui a commencé à Bamako. Il s'agira, confie-t-il, de poursuivre la discussion avec la CEDEAO dans la perspective d'une nouvelle base juridique qui va régir la coopération pour permettre aux populations de continuer leurs activités et de profiter des acquis engrangés ensemble dans le cadre de la CEDEAO. « Nous sommes ici en délégation confédérale, pour affiner les derniers instruments, nous accorder sur l'approche dont la réflexion a commencé depuis Niamey et s'est poursuivie à Bamako. Aujourd'hui, il nous revient donc de les affiner. Les experts ont travaillé, deux jours durant, pour proposer un ordre du jour qui va orienter durant ce dialogue. Un draft d'accord-cadre qui ressort les secteurs prioritaires et la façon dont l'AES veut désormais voir ses rapports avec la CEDEAO. (…). On se rend à Dakar en une seule délégation, portée par une même vision et organisée autour d'un seul discours, d'un seul dialogue : celui de la confédération des États du Sahel », explique le ministre burkinabè des affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. Il a saisi, au passage, le cadre pour battre en brèche et rassurer : « Il y a déjà certaines presses qui commencent à spéculer sur la volonté des trois pays de retourner dans la CEDEAO. C'est l'occasion de rassurer tout le monde, qu'il n'en est rien, et qu'au contraire, la page que nous sommes en train d'ouvrir est celle de la formation de nouveaux rapports, en tenant compte de ces deux entités distinctes, à savoir la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) et la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO), qui constituent désormais deux entités qui vont composer le bloc ouest-africain ». Les ministres malien, Abdoulaye Diop, ... Le ministre malien des affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, Abdoulaye Diop, a insisté sur le fait que les discussions se font dans un « esprit d'ouverture, constructif et de responsabilité de la part de l'AES ». Il rappelle qu'il y a une réalité géographique qui n'a jamais été niée, celle d'appartenance à un même espace, les liens forts qui ont toujours existé entre l'ensemble des peuples et les pays de cet espace, avant de souligner que les discussions avec la CEDEAO « doivent plus que jamais » s'inscrire dans le cadre d'une discussion d'entité à entité (entre l'AES et la CEDEAO). « C'est dans cet esprit que se tiendront les discussions pour trouver un instrument juridique qui va régir les relations entre les deux entités, et ce, dans le souci de préserver les intérêts des populations, et plus largement de l'ensemble des populations des espaces concernés », clarifie le ministre Diop. ...et nigérien Bakary Yaou Sangaré... Pour sa part, le ministre des affaires étrangères, de la coopération et des Nigériens à l'extérieur, Bakary Yaou Sangaré, a d'abord salué la résilience des populations avant de rendre un hommage aux victimes de la crise sécuritaire. « À ce stade, on ne parle plus de victimes. Civils ou militaires, ce sont des martyrs. Quand quelqu'un donne sa vie pour défendre la nation, il est considéré comme un martyr. Il fait partie de la catégorie des gens que Dieu considère comme martyrs. Quand vous mourez en défendant votre famille, votre bien, votre patrie, votre honneur, vous êtes un martyr », évoque le ministre nigérien en charge de la diplomatie. ...ont félicité leur homologue burkinabè, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, pour son leadership à la tête du comité de pilotage de la Confédération AES. « Nous partons à Dakar sereins, convaincus que la confédération n'est contre personne, n'est dressée contre personne ; elle a été créée pour défendre les intérêts de ses populations, pas plus. Celui qui pense qu'elle est contre la CEDEAO ou d'autres institutions se trompe. C'est un chemin, c'est notre chemin, et nous avons jugé opportun de l'emprunter, parce que, pour nous, il n'y en a pas d'autre. Et jusque-là, nous sommes confortables sur cette voie, nous partons à Dakar, pas pour négocier pour retourner à la CEDEAO, nous sommes bien dans notre confédération. Mais plutôt pour voir comment faire en sorte que les deux entités cohabitent pacifiquement et que cette cohabitation soit une valeur ajoutée pour les deux entités », a, à la suite de ses deux homologues, soutenu le ministre des affaires étrangères, de la coopération et des Nigériens à l'extérieur, Bakary Yaou Sangaré. Après la cérémonie d'ouverture, les travaux se sont poursuivis à huis clos. Lire aussi : Coopération : La Confédération AES prépare les futures consultations avec la CEDEAO O.L. Lefaso.net

items.title: Dr. Ekua Amoakoh recounts childhood at Komfo Anokye and how parents pushed her into the medical profession
items.description: Spokesperson for NPP Flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, has recounted how her parents’ insistence led her to study medicine, despite her initial interest in other pursuits. In a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, she spoke about growing up at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, resisting her parents’ career choice and eventually appreciating the value of her medical training. Dr Amoakoh said her childhood was closely tied to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, where her grandmother served as Director of Nursing. She said her family lived in the hospital’s doctors’ flats when she was a baby, making the medical environment a familiar part of her upbringing. “I grew up in a hospital. I grew up in Komfo Anokye. My grandmother was the director of nursing of Komfo Anokye when I was born. So we lived at the flats at the doctors’ flats when I was a baby,” she recounted. She said the environment influenced her parents’ decision about her future career. “That’s all I knew. So when I got to the time to decide what to do, quite frankly, I think that decision was made for me by my parents,” she said. Despite growing up around medical professionals, Dr Amoakoh said she was initially reluctant to follow the same path. She recalled resisting her parents’ decision even after entering medical school. “Initially I kicked against it, or I fought them. Even in medical school, up until about third year, I said, ‘I don’t want to do this. I told you I didn’t want to do this,’” she said. She also recalled sensing that her career had already been decided before she completed secondary school at Holy Child School. She said her parents viewed medicine as a natural choice because of her upbringing and exposure to the profession. Dr Amoakoh offered a glimpse into how her university application was handled, saying her mother completed the application form and presented it to her for her signature. She recalled that she was still in Form Three when her mother arrived with the completed paperwork. “My mom just turns up one day, and then she just brings me the paper to sign. She filled it all out and just brought it to me. All I had to do was sign,” she said. She said she was unhappy at the time because she felt she had little say in the decision about her future. Dr Amoakoh said her interests at the time differed from her parents’ expectations, explaining that she was attracted to wealth creation and the opportunities associated with business. “I always liked the nicer things in life. That’s why I’m a typical capitalist. You will not find me doing anything socialist,” she said. She argued that allowing people to pursue their creativity and create value was important for economic growth. “I don’t actually see anything wrong with trying really hard to make some money. So I was always more attracted to that. And I was like, I grew up in the hospital. I’ve seen all these doctors. No, I want more money,” she recounted. She said those interests contributed to disagreements with her parents over her choice of profession. Although she initially opposed the decision, Dr Amoakoh said she has come to appreciate the experience of studying medicine. She said the demands of medical training can help develop discipline, resilience and the ability to handle challenges, even for those who eventually pursue other careers. “I’m glad they insisted because even if it’s not something you are going to practice or something you are going to use, that whole process of training, I think it can forge any person into a formidable person,” she said. Dr Amoakoh also spoke about her family, revealing that she is the fourth of six children. She said the family had five girls for a long time, with her younger sister Ama close to her in age. “It was an army of girls, and I was number four, and my little sister Ama was five. We were very close in age. So we are almost twins—Irish twins, as she likes to call us. So we grew up very close together,” she said. She added that the family later welcomed a sixth child, a boy.

items.title: Africa Prosperity Dialogues 2027 rescheduled to January 13–15
items.description: The Africa Prosperity Network (APN) has rescheduled the 2027 edition of the Africa Prosperity Dialogues (APD) to January 13–15, moving the event forward by two weeks. The Dialogues were originally scheduled for January 27–29 and will be held at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra. In a statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, the APN said the change was intended to align the event with the African Union’s continental calendar and avoid clashes with key commitments involving African leaders and other participants. The African Union Summit is scheduled for January 30–31, 2027, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with Executive Council meetings preceding it on January 27–28. The revised dates are also intended to accommodate Ramadan, which is expected to begin on the evening of February 7, 2027, subject to the sighting of the moon. Convened under the patronage of President John Dramani Mahama, APD 2027 will bring together African political and business leaders to discuss practical measures to advance free movement, seamless cross-border payments and intra-African trade. The event will be held under the theme, “The Africa We Want Is Borderless. Move Freely. Pay Seamlessly. Trade More.” A key outcome is expected to be the APD Action Compact, a document outlining private-sector priorities, commitments and recommendations to advance Africa’s single market agenda. The Compact is traditionally presented to African leaders during the AU Summit, linking private-sector engagement with continental policy discussions. The APN said the 2027 Dialogues would take place at a significant time for Ghana and the continent, as the country prepares to mark its 70th independence anniversary on March 6, 2027. President Mahama is also expected to be confirmed as Chairperson of the African Union at the forthcoming summit. Deputy Chief of Staff at the Office of the President, Stanislav Xoese Dogbe, said the President viewed APD 2027 as a foundational pillar in a landmark year for Ghana and Africa. The Presidency also sees the event as an opportunity to build intellectual and policy momentum ahead of the AU Summit. The APN has apologised to partners, sponsors and delegates for any inconvenience caused by the revised dates, particularly those who have already begun making travel and other arrangements. Participants have been encouraged to update their calendars and participation plans. The APN Secretariat says it will assist with enquiries relating to the changes. Tickets for the Africa Prosperity Dialogues 2027 are available at africaprosperitynetwork.com .

items.title: Sénégal: à Dakar, une marche contre les féminicides après la mort d'une femme attaquée à l'acide
items.description: Au Sénégal, une nouvelle marche a eu lieu vendredi 16 octobre 2026 pour dire stop aux féminicides. Le 1er octobre, une femme de 40 ans a succombé à ses blessures après avoir été aspergée d'acide par son ex-compagnon à Dakar. Plus de 200 habitants de son quartier ont marché jusqu'à la préfecture de Grand Dakar pour demander justice et l'arrestation du suspect, toujours en fuite.

items.title: NPP will be better prepared for 2028 election security – Ekua Amoakoh
items.description: Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, says the party’s recent national executive elections show that delegates want stronger security arrangements ahead of the 2028 general elections. Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh reflected on the security challenges the party faced during the 2024 elections, describing the situation as chaotic and saying party officials were often unable to protect their polling agents. She said she was in the NPP’s war room during the elections and witnessed reports of violence at various polling stations and collation centres. “All we were seeing was various pockets of violence being directed at our polling agents. There was even an instance in the Upper East Region where some of our polling agents were held at gunpoint to confirm certain results,” she said. “These are all things we saw that day, and there was nothing we could do about it.” Dr Amoakoh said the two major political parties had agreed to leave election security arrangements to the Ghana Police Service rather than rely on party-based security or vigilantism. However, she argued that the police presence at some locations was insufficient to contain disturbances. She cited an example of a collation centre where about 100 people were present, but only around 10 police officers were available, adding that the officers were unarmed. She said the party’s grassroots members and polling agents bore the consequences of the situation, while disputes over some parliamentary results led to re-collation exercises. Dr Amoakoh said the outcome of the NPP’s recent national executive elections suggested that delegates had taken lessons from the 2024 experience and wanted the party to prepare differently. “I think the election results from this past Saturday just show that the party took notice of what happened in 2024. And they want to do something about it,” she said. She added that the results reinforced her view that delegates understood what the party needed at different stages of its development. “It’s clear that we will not be as unprepared security-wise as we were in 2024,” she said. Her comments come as the NPP reorganises its structures following its defeat in the 2024 general elections and prepares for the next polls in 2028. Dr Amoakoh also criticised what she described as the governing National Democratic Congress’ (NDC) interest in the NPP’s internal affairs. She argued that the NDC should focus on governance rather than the opposition party’s internal processes. “I think especially since they have the responsibility of governance, I would expect that they focus on more interesting, more important things. This is like a family matter for the NPP,” she said. Asked why she believed the NDC was paying attention to the NPP’s internal affairs, she suggested that the opposition party’s preparations had unsettled the governing party. “It’s because it has driven some fear into their hearts that, no, this time we will not be pushed around,” she said. Her remarks reflect her own interpretation of the NDC’s response to the NPP’s internal elections. The NPP held its National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on October 3, 2026, as part of its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections. Dr Amoakoh’s comments place election security among the issues she believes the party must address following the challenges reported during the 2024 polls. The party’s preparations will take place against the backdrop of concerns about violence at polling stations and collation centres, as well as disputes over election results.

items.title: Symposium international de sculpture sur granite de Laongo : la 15e édition se tiendra du 2 au 23 novembre 2026
items.description: Le Ministère de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme (MCCAT), à travers la Direction générale de la Culture et des Arts, a officiellement annoncé la tenue de la 15e édition du Symposium international de sculpture sur granite de Laongo, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026, sur le site à Laongo, province de Bassitenga, région de Oubri. L'annonce a été faite au cours d'une conférence de presse animée par le Secrétaire général du MCCAT, Dr Moctar SANFO. ‎À cette occasion, le Secrétaire général a invité les professionnels de l'art, les chercheurs, les universitaires et le public burkinabè sur le site de Laongo, du 2 au 23 novembre 2026, pour la 15e édition du Symposium international de sculpture sur granite de Laongo. Il a souligné que ce Symposium est un rendez-vous biennal majeur de la création sculpturale contemporaine, constituant un espace de rencontre entre artistes, chercheurs et publics et contribuant ainsi à la transmission des savoir-faire et l'enrichissement de notre patrimoine artistique. ‎Il a également expliqué que cette édition poursuit quatre objectifs majeurs >. ‎Le Symposium se déroule, cette année, selon le panorama suivant : – ‎vingt (20) artistes sculpteurs professionnels nationaux et internationaux (venus du Burkina Faso et de plusieurs pays d'Afrique, d'Asie, d'Europe et d'Amérique du Sud) créeront chacun une œuvre en résidence de création ; – quinze (15) jeunes stagiaires bénéficieront d'une formation pratique à la taille de la pierre ; – une trentaine (30) de chercheurs et universitaires sont attendus au colloque scientifique ; – quarante (40) stands d'exposition seront mobilisés dans le cadre de la foire artistique et commerciale « Village Sympo Granite ». Par ailleurs, la tenue du Colloque scientifique international, les 10 et 11 novembre 2026 , permettra d'approfondir la réflexion sur les enjeux d'identité et de patrimoine. Cette 15e édition du Symposium est placée sous le parrainage artistique de l'artiste malien, Abdoulaye KONATÉ, en signe de promotion des échanges et coopérations culturels dans notre espace sous-régional. Le Camarade Mahamoudou OUÉDRAOGO, ancien ministre chargé de la Culture, sera présent en qualité d'invité d'honneur. Des activités comme la foire « Village Sympo Granit», l'édition du catalogue officiel des œuvres de 2024, le cross populaire, la course cycliste et l'accès gratuit devraient permettre une participation active et massive de la population. ‎La conférence de presse a également connu la présence du Haut-commissaire de la province de Bassitenga, Saïdou GUIGMA, de la Directrice générale de la Culture et des Arts, Noëlie CONGO/SALOUKA et du Commissaire général du Symposium, Siriki KY. ‎DCRP/MCCAT

items.title: 80 ans du Rassemblement démocratique africain (RDA): la radicalité du PDG, section guinéenne du RDA [1/2]
items.description: Il y a 80 ans, du 18 au 21 octobre 1946, se tenait le congrès de Bamako, au cours duquel naissait le Rassemblement démocratique africain (RDA), le premier grand mouvement politique panafricain et anticolonialiste. En Guinée, une délégation de leaders politiques guinéens a participé au congrès de Bamako. Peu de temps après, ces responsables ont fondé la section guinéenne du RDA, le Parti démocratique de Guinée (PDG), qui a mené le pays à l’indépendance en 1958. Le fils d’un des acteurs majeurs de l’époque, Mamadou Traoré, dit Ray Autra, nous fait le récit de cette histoire.

Presse privée : 79 structures bénéficient de la subvention de l’État au titre de 2026
items.description: Le Ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO a présidé, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle de remise des chèques aux bénéficiaires de la subvention annuelle de l’État à la presse privée, au titre de l’exercice 2026. Cette année, 79 structures, dont 77 entreprises de presse privée et deux organisations professionnelles des médias, ont été retenues pour bénéficier d’une enveloppe globale de 320 millions de FCFA. Pour le Ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO , cette subvention traduit la volonté du Gouvernement de poursuivre son accompagnement au secteur privé de la presse, dont le rôle demeure essentiel dans l’information des citoyens, la sensibilisation des populations et la consolidation de la cohésion sociale. Il a invité les bénéficiaires à faire preuve de responsabilité dans la gestion des ressources allouées et à renforcer la professionnalisation de leurs entreprises. Il a également souligné la nécessité d’une presse engagée, crédible et respectueuse de l’éthique et de la déontologie journalistiques, particulièrement dans le contexte sécuritaire actuel. La Directrice générale du Fonds d’Appui au Sport et à la Presse privée (FASP) « Wassa Bondo », Ida OUEDRAOGO/PARE, a, pour sa part, présenté le bilan du processus de sélection et de répartition. Elle a rappelé les exigences de transparence, de bonne gestion et de reddition des comptes. À travers cette initiative, le Gouvernement entend consolider son partenariat avec la presse privée et contribuer au renforcement de ses capacités opérationnelles. DCRP/MCCAT

items.title: Frente Amplio y Podemos fracasan en su intento de pactar una papeleta única para el 29-N
items.description: Tras un pulso muy duro librado en los últimos diez días, las izquierdas han naufragado este viernes en su intento por lograr un acuerdo estatal para que haya una única papeleta a las elecciones generales del 29-N. En una jornada que volvió a ser agónica, con llamamientos de muchas voces al acuerdo, largos silencios de las direcciones de los partidos reunidas toda la tarde y ofertas in extremis , Podemos y el Frente Amplio (IU, Más Madrid, Comuns y Movimiento Sumar) han llegado al entendimiento solo en Comunidad Valenciana y Canarias. En Madrid, el elector situado más a la izquierda podrá elegir finalmente entre las papeletas encabezadas por Irene Montero, que irrumpió como aspirante a la presidencia ya antes de que Pedro Sánchez anunciara el adelanto electoral y contará con el respaldo de Gabriel Rufián; y la que lidera el diputado autonómico de Más Madrid Emilio Delgado , que tendrá a Ada Colau como candidata principal de la coalición por Barcelona. items.title: El PSOE y el Frente Amplio alcanzan un pacto nacional de listas conjuntas al Senado
items.description: La izquierda irá unida al Senado en las elecciones generales del 29-N. La operación ideada a marchas forzadas para arrebatar la mayoría absoluta al PP en la Cámara Alta ha logrado lo que hace una semana parecía imposible: una coalición del PSOE en 45 provincias con otras fuerzas progresistas del Frente Amplio, según fuentes de la negociación. Bajo la denominación “Senado de Progreso”, la integrarán los socialistas, IU, Movimiento Sumar, Compromís, Más Madrid, Chunta Aragonesista, Batzarre y Més. Aunque no entra Podemos, no se descarta que pueda proponer nombres con el beneplácito del resto de fuerzas. Con este acuerdo, que no se aplicará en Cataluña y Canarias salvo en La Gomera, la alianza de izquierdas —que se ha demorado por la incertidumbre de si Podemos entraría en el Frente Amplio— confía en ser la primera fuerza en numerosas provincias, desbancando al PP. La combinación de la suma de las izquierdas, evitando que decenas de miles de votos se queden sin representación, y la división de la derecha, donde Vox subiría en detrimento del PP, tendría como resultado una recomposición de la cámara territorial totalmente diferente a la de esta legislatura, en la que el PP ha utilizado al Senado como su ariete legislativo contra el Gobierno. items.title: Top global climate science body suspends meeting without deal on major review timeline
items.description: By Sudarshan Varadhan Oct 16 (Reuters) - A meeting of the members of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was suspended without an agreement on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet, the IPCC said on Friday. The impasse over the timeline, which has lasted nearly three years, could leave countries to decide the next phase of climate action without consensus on critical issues, including the extent to which some global warming might be reversible.

items.title: Livestream: Newsfile discusses GH¢49.72m evacuation cost, EC appointments and Obuasi SHTS abuse case
items.description: JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile , on Saturday, October 17, examine four major national issues that have dominated public debate over the past week. Hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, the programme will discuss the GH¢49.72 million spent evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa, controversy over appointments to the Electoral Commission (EC), allegations of sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), and the dismissal of a GH¢15 million defamation suit filed by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin. The programme airs from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms. GH¢49.72m evacuation bill under scrutiny The programme will examine questions surrounding the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa following xenophobic attacks. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has said GH¢38.84 million was used for chartered flights, air tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation and medical care, while GH¢10.80 million went towards reintegration support and transportation allowances. The government contributed GH¢33.72 million, while businessman Ibrahim Mahama’s company, Engineers and Planners, donated GH¢16 million. The Minority in Parliament has demanded a detailed breakdown of the expenditure, including the cost per evacuee. The Ministry has reportedly submitted a 200-page report in response to a Right to Information request. Mr Ablakwa has also requested an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken by successive governments since 2017. The discussion will consider the expenditure, the documentation supporting it and the accountability questions raised by the Minority. EC appointments raise questions about neutrality The programme will also consider the controversy surrounding President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission. Madam Agbenyo’s previous role as an NDC manifesto spokesperson has prompted concerns about the political neutrality of the electoral management body. The New Patriotic Party has called for her appointment to be withdrawn, citing her perceived political affiliation. Minister of State in charge of Government Communications Felix Kwakye Ofosu has defended the appointments, arguing that institutional changes can also address perceived imbalances in state institutions. He has also pointed to appointments made under the previous administration. The NDC maintains that Madam Agbenyo has the qualifications and integrity required for the role. The discussion will examine the concerns surrounding political affiliations and the standards expected of officials entrusted with overseeing elections. Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations Allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students will form another part of the programme. Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni has reported that the number of students alleging abuse has risen to 16. The Ghana Education Service has suspended the headmaster pending investigations. Reports have also linked him to the National Democratic Congress in Juaben, where he is said to have served as constituency secretary and sought to contest the chairmanship. Some parents have reportedly alleged that they were being pressured to withdraw their complaints. Parliament’s Committee on Human Rights has condemned the alleged abuse and called for speedy action. The programme will examine the allegations, the ongoing investigations and questions about whether warning signs were missed or concerns were not acted upon. The allegations remain subject to investigation and must be established through due process. Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15m suit dismissed The final issue will be the Accra High Court’s dismissal of the GH¢15 million defamation suit filed by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin against Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi. The court struck out the case on October 14, ruling that the writ of summons was “incurably defective and incompetent”. The ruling centred on compliance with Order 57 Rule 2 of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), which sets out requirements for actions involving defamation. The court’s decision was procedural and did not determine whether Mr Gyamfi’s remarks were defamatory. The suit followed comments Mr Gyamfi made on JoyNews’ Newsfile in August 2026, when he described Mr Afenyo-Markin as an “extortionist”. The programme will examine the implications of the ruling and whether the Minority Leader’s legal team will seek to correct the defects and pursue the case again. Newsfile airs on Saturday, October 17, from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms. WATCH THE LIVE SHOW BELOW \

items.title: Ablakwa to face Newsfile questions on BRICS bid and GH¢49.7m evacuation cost
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa will face questions on Ghana’s bid to join the BRICS economic bloc and the GH¢49.7 million spent evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa when he appears on JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile , on Saturday, October 17. Mr Ablakwa will be interviewed by host Samson Lardy Anyenini on the two issues, which have sparked debate over Ghana’s foreign policy direction and the cost of protecting citizens abroad. The interview comes after Cabinet approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, a grouping of emerging economies. Mr Ablakwa announced the decision during a joint press briefing with India’s External Affairs Minister, Dr S. Jaishankar, in Accra on October 6. He said membership could help Ghana diversify its international partnerships and expand opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation. “BRICS offers us that opportunity to have options in our development agenda, and you want to have options,” he said. Mr Ablakwa said Ghana was pursuing sustainable economic growth, industrialisation and greater control over its natural resources, adding that the country wanted to move away from continued dependence on exporting raw materials. Dr Jaishankar welcomed Ghana’s interest but noted that the decision would require collective consideration by BRICS members. The proposal has drawn scrutiny from the Minority in Parliament, which has called for an urgent briefing on the geopolitical and national-interest implications of the move. Samuel Abu Jinapor, Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, has questioned why Ghana is pursuing full membership rather than a partner-country arrangement similar to Nigeria’s. GH¢49.7m evacuation cost faces questions The second major issue will be the GH¢49.7 million spent evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa following xenophobic attacks. According to Mr Ablakwa, the exercise cost GH¢49,721,786, with the government contributing GH¢33.7 million and Engineers and Planners, owned by businessman Ibrahim Mahama, donating GH¢16 million. He said each evacuee received GH¢5,000 as a reintegration grant and GH¢500 for travel and transportation. “The lives protected and the dignity of Ghanaians far outweighs the cost,” Mr Ablakwa said in defence of the expenditure. The spending has, however, prompted calls from the Minority for a detailed breakdown of the costs, including the amount spent per evacuee. The Minority Caucus on the Foreign Affairs Committee boycotted a planned briefing by the Minister, leading the Committee Chairman to reschedule the meeting. The Majority Caucus has defended the expenditure, insisting that no public funds are missing. Committee Chairman Dr Alfred Okoe Vanderpuije has said the Ministry submitted a report supported by receipts and other documentation covering the operation. Mr Ablakwa has also voluntarily requested an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken by successive governments since 2017. Newsfile airs from 8:00am on Saturday, October 17 , on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

items.title: The Blog Post That Set the AI World on Fire
items.description: For the past 24 hours, Silicon Valley has been obsessed with a 26,000-word blog post by the AI researcher Nick Cammarata. The document has been called the “the most important essay,” “the most important result,” and “the single best piece of news” of the year , or in the history of AI research—or, perhaps, ever. Even OpenAI CEO Sam Altman lauded it. Cammarata makes a series of bold, almost astonishing claims about the nature of AI that, if true, would upend some of his industry’s basic assumptions about the very thing it is building. And after months of AI-hacking sprees and mounting public backlash against the industry, many people see Cammarata as offering a glimmer of hope when it comes to not just understanding but also controlling the technology being unleashed on the world. Boiled down, Cammarata’s main contention is that generative-AI models are not actually black boxes, contrary to the common perception that these systems are so big and labyrinthine as to be nearly impenetrable. In fact, Cammarata argues, there is a relatively clear path toward understanding them. If that’s the case, the material significance could be tremendous: It would provide a way to map AI models’ inner workings and, in turn, perhaps prevent them from wreaking all sorts of harm—autonomously hacking companies and sovereign nations, encouraging users’ delusions, appearing to deceive AI researchers themselves. There is an entire field of research, called “mechanistic interpretability,” devoted to the study of just this. The argument is just as important as the person making it. Cammarata, a former OpenAI employee, is a respected figure in his field. Years ago, he played a key role in establishing the opposite claim, which is now common wisdom: that neural networks, the software architecture that generative AI is built on, are impossible, or at least very difficult, to understand. In this new essay, Cammarata, who now works at the AI-research company Goodfire, essentially says that he and his entire field have been wrong ever since. “The claims here are viscerally shocking,” one observer wrote . Or, as another wrote on X, they are “big big big big.” [ Read: Imagine every AI agent on Earth buying the same cheap paper towels ] Neural networks, inspired by the human brain, consist of layered connections among individual nodes, or “neurons,” that activate and send information to one another when responding to a query. Earlier research, including Cammarata’s, established that individual machine neurons can activate in response to many different, unrelated topics—for instance, one neuron can correspond to images of cat faces, cat legs, and the front of cars. Nobody was sure why this happened, but one explanation was that, because AI models contain far more information than they have neurons, they have to repurpose these nodes. Regardless, the basic units of an AI model having seemingly arbitrary, multitudinous functions would make it very difficult to understand what is going on under the hood. Cammarata now thinks that individual neurons can be understood and that each has a self-consistent function. Neural networks are not “tangled knots,” he wrote, but “clean.” He found that the cat-face and car-face neuron, for instance, was actually responding to things with a V-shape—including V-shaped flames and jets of water. This would make AI’s internal mechanisms relatively straightforward and predictable rather than mysterious and nebulous. And if we can harness that understanding, some people in the industry believe, AI will be much less likely to go haywire and, say, kill us all. “This is truly one of the greatest cases for optimism in years!” the OpenAI researcher Adam Majmudar wrote on X. Not everyone agrees with Cammarata. For one, his 26,000 words were merely a “working hypothesis” for a “forthcoming technical paper” and were thus hard, on a technical level, to evaluate. And the neural networks he studied most closely were vision models, which are generally simpler and better understood than the language models underlying ChatGPT and Claude. Cammarata could be mistaken, or he could be overstating his case. The blog post isn’t peer-reviewed, and the forthcoming paper probably won’t be, either, as is typical in the field. The research itself is something of a black box. (Cammarata, who did not immediately respond to a request for comment, wrote on X earlier today that he appreciates all of the discussion and that his approach “seems promising so far” for “bigger modern language models.”) Discussions of Cammarata’s essay have revealed philosophical rifts. “This is interesting work, but I don’t think it’s a significant update to the big picture,” Neel Nanda, who leads mechanistic interpretability at Google DeepMind, wrote in his appraisal of Cammarata’s findings. Even if researchers could approximate the function of every neuron in Claude Mythos 5.1 or GPT-6 Astra, that’s not the same as understanding how they connect and how the network works as a whole. Physicists have good models of atoms and interatomic interactions, but they cannot from first principles explain or predict every physical event (hence unpredictable extreme weather or, for that matter, the notion of free will). You know all of your friends from school, various workplaces, and the local softball league, but you can’t always know whether they’ll get along at your birthday party. More to the point, insights into the inner workings of an AI model will not necessarily produce insights into how to make the technology more reliable. Interpretability may be necessary to build safer AI models, but it is by no means sufficient. If generative-AI models are actually legible under the hood, that would undoubtedly help make the technology safer. But many people in Silicon Valley, and especially employees at OpenAI, are discussing Cammarata’s blog post with a breathless enthusiasm that echoes Silicon Valley’s long track record of easy technical solutions and grand promises—an attitude that belies its mixed record on following through. Any research finding that pertains to AI safety will require an industry chasing multitrillion-dollar public offerings to slow down and take a long, hard look at itself. Perhaps even more concerning than an unintelligible superintelligence is the fact that a group of companies openly state that they don’t really know what they are building—and then continue to push that technology to extremes anyway. If Cammarata is correct, AI companies will have to work with one another, outside auditors, and governments to figure out how to translate such a breakthrough into safe and reliable products. And right now, absent any serious regulation, nobody can decide to take such action other than the companies themselves. All of which suggests that the real black boxes are OpenAI and Anthropic themselves.
